pr_body:
This adds `ECDiffieHellman` functionality to `X509Certificate2`. In addition, this also adds arbitrary `SubjectPublicKeyInfo` support for `PublicKey`.

This also makes some under-the-hood changes. Previously, we were always able to know what type of algorithm was used with a given certificate based on the certificate SPKI's OID. In the case of id-ecPublicKey, this is not true anymore. Other plumbing changes include changes to support `ImportFromPem` on `X509Certificate2`.

Work left to be done:

- [x] XML documentation
- [x] Windows PFX tests

Closes #413

Hm. CNG is behaving differently between Win10 and Win8.1/7. I suppose this is related to CNG's strong opinion that EC keys are either ECDH or ECDSA.
@bartonjs I think I fixed the Windows 7 / 8.1 key import problem. Does the change in 2d4fda5076435e90ccf8bfea22f481d3795ee4af make sense?

>  Does the change in 2d4fda5 make sense?

Depends on your definition of "make sense" :smile:.  Apparently the private keys default to ECDH but the public keys were defaulting to ECDSA, and whatever lookup it did in the CryptFindOID universe returned multiple hits, ECDSA first... and that flag says "if something can't encrypt, I don't want it".. and while ECDH can't encrypt, it's purpose is eventually encryption, so it's marked as "encryption".  Does any of that make sense? Not especially :smile:.

Does the code read cleanly? Sure.  Does it make tests pass? Apparently :smile:.
@bartonjs thanks as always for the thoughtful feedback. I think I have addressed all of the points you have made so far.
Guessing macOS is going to blow up with a bad DSA at usage time, not import time. No idea what what it is actually doing with an 8-bit DSA key.

> Guessing macOS is going to blow up with a bad DSA at usage time, not import time. No idea what what it is actually doing with an 8-bit DSA key.

Well, p is 0, so that's a 0-bit key, no? :smile:.


issue_context.title: API Enhancement: ECDiffieHellman X509 certificate management gaps

review_comments: I think flipping these will fix the Windows problems. IIRC, ECDH keys can do ECDH or ECDSA, but ECDSA keys can't do ECDH.

Is it even possible to get into this second EcPublicKey block on any OS?  For Linux and macOS it's just an ECC key.  For Windows I think the only thing that might stand a chance of failing this test is a Montgomery curve (Curve25519), since (IIRC) Montgomery curves are only allowed to do ECDH on Windows (I don't remember if that fails at import time, or signing time).

The `GetECDsaPublicKey` and friends take in to account of the certificate's key usage. So if the cert has a keyUsage of only `keyAgreement`, `GetECDsaPublicKey` will return null and we'll end up in here.
This was pulled from `ECDsaCertificateExtensions` and changed to accept the `ECParameters`, and renamed to be clear this is only comparing the public properties of `ECParameters`.

Do you see value any of these extra tests:

* new CertificateRequest(ecdsa, ...) with KeyAgreement KU makes for a valid ECDH/invalid ECDSA cert
* new CertificateRequest(new PublicKey(ecdh), ...) without KeyAgreement makes the cert valid for ECDSA and ECDH
* Other sorts of "flexibility has increased" / "the output key can't be used to rerun this test".

The first bullet is actually interesting in that CreateSelfSigned will... probably... fail? Since CopyWithPrivateKey... should... fail?

> CreateSelfSigned will... probably... fail? Since CopyWithPrivateKey... should... fail?

Yeah. It fails with

> The provided key does not match the public key algorithm for this certificate.

This is already existing behavior. I think the behavior is... reasonable, but maybe could be something we have additional validation on in `CreateSelfSigned` so the exception is clearer. If anything it seems not quite right that the result is an `ArgumentException`. I don't think folks should reasonably expect to create a cert with an ECDSA cert and get an ECDH back out.
Actually we throw an `ArgumentException` in a lot of other cases for `Create`, so maybe it's closer to "okay" than I thought.

> I don't think folks should reasonably expect to create a cert with an ECDSA cert and get an ECDH back out.

I agree, but if it works now (especially if it works in already shipped versions) we probably want to keep it working.

> but maybe could be something we have additional validation on in CreateSelfSigned so the exception is clearer.

I'm amenable to that (but it probably makes more sense as a followup change).

> Actually we throw an ArgumentException in a lot of other cases for Create, so maybe it's closer to "okay" than I thought.

We could (in a change other than this one) try to clean those up, too.

>  if it works now (especially if it works in already shipped versions)

It does not nor did it. Opened #42751 to improve it later.

Well, the thing I'm concerned works and could potentially not in the future is Create, not CreateSelfSigned.  (But it'd require us saving a lot more state than we currently do, so it's not super likely to break)
Is this check still appropriate for ECDH?  Can't it use id-ecDH or id-ecPublicKey?
Will XML doc edits eventually propogate back up to docs, or do I need to open a new PR after this one to modify existing docs?

> Will XML doc edits eventually propogate back up to docs, or do I need to open a new PR after this one to modify existing docs?

Unfortunately, they don't propagate.  There's an import tool that imports the doc comments to the docs site for members which are entirely lacking documentation; but further changes happen in that repository and don't flow back to here... so updates here can't sensibly flow back to the docs site.

So, yeah, it'll need a manual PR to the docs site.  (I don't think it would need any sort of "starting in .NET 6.0" for this particular change)
